Summary: In SCOP 1.69, PA1492 (1t1j) and nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase (1f8y) were unrelated in the hierarchy at every level below class. PA1492 had its own singleton fold, superfamily, and family (c.137 / c.137.1 / c.137.1.1, all named 'Hypothetical protein PA1492'), while 1f8y sat in the Flavodoxin-like fold c.23, superfamily c.23.14 'N-deoxyribosyltransferase', family c.23.14.1. They shared only class c (alpha and beta proteins, a/b), which carries no homology claim. In the current SCOPe release (2.08, the public release reported by the service; freeze 2021-07-28, latest periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16), PA1492 has been merged into the 1f8y lineage: both domains are in fold c.23 Flavodoxin-like and superfamily c.23.14, now renamed 'N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like' (sunid 52309). They remain in different families: 1f8y is c.23.14.1 'N-deoxyribosyltransferase' (sunid 52310; protein 'Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase', Lactobacillus leichmannii) and PA1492 is c.23.14.2 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (sunid 110461, Pseudomonas aeruginosa). So the relationship moved from 'no asserted relationship beyond class' to 'same superfamily, different family', i.e. SCOPe now asserts probable common ancestry between them but not the closer family-level relationship. The former fold c.137 and superfamily c.137.1 no longer appear in the PA1492 lineage.

Release-by-release facts retrieved: 1.69: d1t1ja_/d1t1jb_ (sunids 106249/106250) = c.137.1.1; d1f8ya_/d1f8yb_ (sunids 31395/31396) = c.23.14.1. 1.71 and 1.73: d1t1ja_/d1t1jb_ = c.23.14.2 (the merge had already occurred by 1.71, i.e. the SCOP 1.71-1.73 period described by Andreeva et al. 2008). 2.08: d1t1ja1 (1t1j A:1-118) and d1t1jb1 (B:1-118) = c.23.14.2; d1f8ya_/d1f8yb_ = c.23.14.1. The compare tool reports the lowest shared node in 2.08 as superfamily c.23.14 (relationship 'same_superfamily'), with no homology warnings, inconsistencies, or heterogeneity annotations on either domain. The PA1492 sunids (family 110461, protein 110462, species 110463, domains 106249/106250) are stable across releases; only their parents changed, which is what makes this a reclassification rather than a new entry.

Additional change in SCOPe: in 2.08, 1t1j chains have been split so that the N-terminal expression-tag residues (A:0-0, B:-6-0) are separate class l 'Artifacts / Tags' domains d1t1ja2 and d1t1jb2 (l.1.1.1). The homology section flags these with 'artifact_not_homology_evidence'. They are not part of the PA1492 domain and carry no evolutionary meaning; the real PA1492 domain boundary in 2.08 is A:1-118 / B:1-118, versus whole-chain in 1.69-1.73.

Evolutionary strength and limits: Shared superfamily c.23.14 means SCOPe asserts probable common ancestry between PA1492 and nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase; the shared Flavodoxin-like fold c.23 alone would only indicate structural similarity. Different families mean SCOPe does not claim the close sequence/functional relationship implied by family membership. Superfamily placement does not establish that PA1492 is a deoxyribosyltransferase or binds nucleosides; its SCOPe annotation is still 'Structural genomics target' with protein name 'Hypothetical protein', so function transfer from 1f8y is not supported by SCOPe data and would need biochemical or ligand-binding evidence. The API shows that the classification changed and when, but does not record the curators' rationale (the sequence, structure, or literature argument Andreeva et al. gave); that rationale was not verified from the retrieved data. 1f8y should not be treated as an interchangeable structural template for PA1492 at the residue level without an inspected alignment, which was not retrieved here.

Summary: In SCOP 1.69, PA1492 (1t1j) and nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase (1f8y) were unrelated in the hierarchy at every level below class. PA1492 had its own singleton fold, superfamily, and family (c.137 / c.137.1 / c.137.1.1, all named 'Hypothetical protein PA1492'), while 1f8y sat in the Flavodoxin-like fold c.23, superfamily c.23.14 'N-deoxyribosyltransferase', family c.23.14.1. They shared only class c (alpha and beta proteins, a/b), which carries no homology claim. In the current SCOPe release (2.08, the public release reported by the service; freeze 2021-07-28, latest periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16), PA1492 has been merged into the 1f8y lineage: both domains are in fold c.23 Flavodoxin-like and superfamily c.23.14, now renamed 'N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like' (sunid 52309). They remain in different families: 1f8y is c.23.14.1 'N-deoxyribosyltransferase' (sunid 52310; protein 'Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase', Lactobacillus leichmannii) and PA1492 is c.23.14.2 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (sunid 110461, Pseudomonas aeruginosa). So the relationship moved from 'no asserted relationship beyond class' to 'same superfamily, different family', i.e. SCOPe now asserts probable common ancestry between them but not the closer family-level relationship. The former fold c.137 and superfamily c.137.1 no longer appear in the PA1492 lineage.

Release-by-release facts retrieved: 1.69: d1t1ja_/d1t1jb_ (sunids 106249/106250) = c.137.1.1; d1f8ya_/d1f8yb_ (sunids 31395/31396) = c.23.14.1. 1.71 and 1.73: d1t1ja_/d1t1jb_ = c.23.14.2 (the merge had already occurred by 1.71, i.e. the SCOP 1.71-1.73 period described by Andreeva et al. 2008). 2.08: d1t1ja1 (1t1j A:1-118) and d1t1jb1 (B:1-118) = c.23.14.2; d1f8ya_/d1f8yb_ = c.23.14.1. The compare tool reports the lowest shared node in 2.08 as superfamily c.23.14 (relationship 'same_superfamily'), with no homology warnings, inconsistencies, or heterogeneity annotations on either domain. The PA1492 sunids (family 110461, protein 110462, species 110463, domains 106249/106250) are stable across releases; only their parents changed, which is what makes this a reclassification rather than a new entry.

Additional change in SCOPe: in 2.08, 1t1j chains have been split so that the N-terminal expression-tag residues (A:0-0, B:-6-0) are separate class l 'Artifacts / Tags' domains d1t1ja2 and d1t1jb2 (l.1.1.1). The homology section flags these with 'artifact_not_homology_evidence'. They are not part of the PA1492 domain and carry no evolutionary meaning; the real PA1492 domain boundary in 2.08 is A:1-118 / B:1-118, versus whole-chain in 1.69-1.73.

Evolutionary strength and limits: Shared superfamily c.23.14 means SCOPe asserts probable common ancestry between PA1492 and nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase; the shared Flavodoxin-like fold c.23 alone would only indicate structural similarity. Different families mean SCOPe does not claim the close sequence/functional relationship implied by family membership. Superfamily placement does not establish that PA1492 is a deoxyribosyltransferase or binds nucleosides; its SCOPe annotation is still 'Structural genomics target' with protein name 'Hypothetical protein', so function transfer from 1f8y is not supported by SCOPe data and would need biochemical or ligand-binding evidence. The API shows that the classification changed and when, but does not record the curators' rationale (the sequence, structure, or literature argument Andreeva et al. gave); that rationale was not verified from the retrieved data. 1f8y should not be treated as an interchangeable structural template for PA1492 at the residue level without an inspected alignment, which was not retrieved here.
